Is a cell's DNA copy exact? No. DNA Copying and Variation, Class 10 Biology.

• The body design blueprint is DNA, in the chromosomes of the nucleus
• A cell copies its DNA, then divides into two new cells
• No biochemical reaction is 100% accurate, so every copy varies a little
• Imagine warming water: most would die, a few heat-resistant variants survive and grow
• Variation helps a species survive, and it is the foundation for evolution
